published_results.claim: **Purpose:** Reduce static prompt overhead by ~40% for models with context windows under 200K tokens.
published_results.metric: Static prompt overhead reduction from context-window-aware prompt thinning (executor/planner prompts on sub-200K models)

published_results.claim: - **Changed:** Thin orchestrator pattern — commands delegate to workflows, reducing command file size ~75%.

summary: gsd-core publishes no results on task success, output quality or end-to-end agent cost. Its measured numbers are static prompt-size reductions from two offline token-count scripts with committed JSON baselines: with the opt-in `workflow.compact_content` mode (off by default), the six spine/detail workflow splits come to 15.5% fewer tokens (113,676 to 96,055) and the 32 compact variant files to 21.91% fewer (122,467 to 95,637), counted with gpt-tokenizer as a stand-in for Claude's tokenizer and without a check that output quality holds; both rerun deterministically with `npm run benchmark:compact-content` and `npm run benchmark:compact-content-variants`. The '~40%' static-overhead reduction from prompt thinning and the '~75%' smaller command files are stated without a measurement.
result_focus_note: manual classification of published_results: outcome = does the tool do its job; engineering = speed of the software itself
